newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIA WIN AVERTS ARGENTINA WALKOUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIA WIN AVERTS ARGENTINA WALKOUT.

text.p: Copa America hosts Bolivia averted a possible walkout by furious Argentina when they beat Uruguay to win their first round group Wednesday.

Argentina coach Daniel Passarella had threatened to take his team home because of an alteration in the rules that would have changed the venue of their quarter-final to high altitude La Paz if Bolivia had finished second in their group.

The Argentine threat dominated the day in the trouble-hit competition, overshadowing the action on the field where Bolivia and Peru joined Brazil, Argentina and Ecuador in the quarter-finals. Paraguay also went through without kicking a ball thanks to the intricacies of the rules.
Argentina had drawn 1-1 with Paraguay to finish second in group A Tuesday, earning a quarter-final tie against the second-placed team in group B, which includes Bolivia.
But earlier Tuesday, the Copa America organisers had announced that if Bolivia finished second in group B, the quarter-final in question would be switched from Sucre, its original venue, to La Paz.
Sucre is 2,700 metres above sea level, only slightly higher than Argentina's first round venue of Cochbamba, but La Paz lies at 3,600 metres and is a dreaded venue for visiting teams.
"I'm not going to La Paz. I don't care about the consequences when I believe I am right, when I defend my ideas, my principles and my convictions," Passarella said.
"I've cooled down a bit since last night but the fact that I've cooled down hasn't changed my way of thinking," he said.

"The simple truth is that you cannot change the rules in the middle of the tournament," said Passarella, who found out about the alteration when a reporter asked his opinion about it during a media conference.
He got full backing from his players. "Daniel has our unanimous backing, the rules must be stuck too," he said, said midfielder Marcelo Gallardo.

Passarella, who has brought a second-string team to the Copa, is already angry at the timing of the competition, which is crammed between the region's World Cup qualifying matches. He also claims the World Cup qualifying competition itself is too long.

He has sore memories of Argentina's last trip to La Paz when they were beaten 2-1 by Bolivia in a World Cup qualifier in April. Argentina had two players sent off and were involved in a brawl that held up play for ten minutes.
Later Wednesday, Eduardo Deluca, secretary-general of the South American Football Confederation, said Passarella had agreed to play in La Paz if necessary.

"I met Passarella, I apologised for the way things had been done and he changed his decision," said Deluca, who is an Argentine. He added: "It's not the Bolivians' fault that they are in a geographical situation which places them at altitude."
In the event, Bolivia solved the problem by beating Uruguay 1-0 to finish top of their group and send Argentina to Sucre, where they meet Peru, 2-0 winners over Venezuela earlier in the day.

Uruguay finished third with three points and this put Paraguay, who finished third in group A with four points, into the quarter-finals as only the worst of the three third-placed teams goes out in the first round.
Uruguay were left waiting for the outcome of Thursday's Mexico-Costa Rica and Brazil-Colombia matches in group C to know if they progress.
Their game against Bolivia showed all the difficulties of playing at such a height, as Bolivia won almost every loose ball, even when the Uruguayan player was clear favourite to get there first.
Julio Cesar Baldivieso's 30th minute strike was the only goal but the Bolivians totally dominated the game, missing an incredible number of chances and striking the woodwork three times.

After the public apathy which struck their first two matches, played in a stadium barely one-third full, Bolivia had the backing of a 35,000 crowd after organisers decided to let in two for the price of one.
In Santa Cruz, the world champions' defensive worries continued with coach Mario Zagallo announcing yet another change in the central defence pairing for Thursday.

Having tried Celio Silva-Marcio Santos, Celio Silva-Aldair and Goncalves-Aldair in recent matches, he reverted to Goncalves-Aldair after a shaky showing by Celio Silva and Aldair in Monday's 3-2 win over Mexico.
